n: Alma now narrates in first person. As he and Amulek begin preaching in Ammonihah, the people immediately argue with him.

f.g: Mormon switches to quoting Alma’s own record; chapters 9–14 are largely in Alma’s voice.

n: They scoff: why should we believe one man, even if he claims the earth will pass away?
Alma notes the irony: they mentioned the earth passing away as an absurd idea, not realizing it is actually true.
They add that they wouldn’t believe even if he prophesied their great city would be destroyed in a single day — which is exactly what later happens.
They could not imagine God doing such things, because their hearts were hard and their necks stiff.

f.g: Stubborn, refusing to bow — an image from oxen resisting the yoke.

n: They mock God himself: what kind of God would send only one man to announce such great things?

f.w: no more authority than one man
f.g: Amulek will soon become the second witness.

n: They move to seize Alma but are held back, and he testifies boldly.
Alma rebukes them as a wicked generation that has quickly forgotten the traditions and commandments of their fathers.
Do you not remember that God brought Lehi out of Jerusalem and led them through the wilderness?

f.w: brought out of Jerusalem by the hand of God

n: Have you forgotten how often God saved our ancestors from enemies, even their own brothers?
Without God’s matchless power, mercy, and patience, the Nephites would long ago have been wiped out and possibly lost forever.
God commands repentance — without it no one can inherit his kingdom, and this people will be destroyed.
Alma quotes the covenant promise to Lehi: keep the commandments and prosper; break them and be cut off from the Lord’s presence.

f.w: ye shall prosper in the land

n: The Lamanites show the truth of this: disobedience cut them off from the Lord’s presence.

f.w: cut off from the presence of the Lord

n: Yet it will be easier for the Lamanites, both now and at judgment, than for these Nephites if they don’t repent — because they sin against greater light.

f.w: more tolerable for them in the day of judgment

n: The Lamanites have many promises because their ignorance came from their fathers’ false traditions. The Lord will be merciful and preserve them.
Someday many Lamanites will believe and be saved, for the Lord is merciful to all who call on him — fulfilled within this very book through the sons of Mosiah.

f.w: many of them will be saved

n: But if these Nephites persist in sin, the Lamanites will come upon them unexpectedly and destroy them.

f.w: the Lamanites shall be sent upon you

n: God would rather let all the Nephites be destroyed than let them live in sin after receiving so much light. Greater knowledge brings greater accountability.

f.w: so much light and so much knowledge

n: The Nephites had been favored above every nation, receiving knowledge of past, present, and future according to their faith.
Alma lists their spiritual gifts: the Spirit, angels, the Lord’s voice, prophecy, revelation, tongues, preaching, the Holy Ghost, and translation.
He lists their temporal blessings too: rescue from Jerusalem, famine, disease, enemies, and bondage, and finally great wealth.

f.w: brought out of bondage time after time

n: If a people so blessed sins against such light, it will go far easier for the Lamanites.

f.w: contrary to the light and knowledge

n: The Lord’s promises extend to the Lamanites, but rebellious Nephites have been warned of utter destruction.
That is why angels have visited many people, sending them to cry repentance, for the kingdom of heaven is near.

f.w: the Lord has sent his angel

n: Soon the Son of God will come in glory — full of grace, fairness, truth, patience, and mercy, quick to hear and answer his people’s prayers.

f.w: the Only Begotten of the Father

n: He comes to redeem those who are baptized with repentance and faith in his name.
Prepare the way, for everyone will reap what they’ve sown: salvation through Christ for the righteous, damnation under the devil’s captivity for the wicked.

f.w: reap a reward of their works

n: Alma states that this is the angel’s message to the people.
Despite his warnings, Alma calls them beloved brothers. He urges them to show real repentance, for they are lost and fallen.

f.w: works which are meet for repentance

n: The people are furious at being called hard-hearted and stiffnecked.
Angry at being called lost and fallen, they try to seize and imprison Alma.
The Lord prevents them from taking him at that time.

f.w: the Lord did not suffer them

n: Then Amulek stands to preach. Mormon notes only part of his words are recorded.

f.w: a part of his words are written
